briefs.explicit:
MISSION BRIEF M-004
Units: metres, seconds, kilograms. Time starts at t = 0 when every robot leaves its start location.

Locations (x, y, zone):
- base: (0, 0), outdoor
- warehouse roof: (-8, 99), roof
- office roof: (65, 143), roof
- control room: (-59, -3), indoor
- workshop: (-129, -147), indoor
- gate 2: (85, 42), outdoor
- water tank: (-41, -33), outdoor
- parking lot: (138, 139), outdoor

Robots:
- D1 (quadcopter): starts at base. Flies in straight lines at 8.5 m/s; can reach outdoor and roof locations, not indoor ones. Equipment: camera, cargo carrier (max 2 kg), thermal camera. Endurance: 900 s, including the return to its start.
- M1 (mobile_manipulator): starts at base. Drives on the road grid (travel distance = |dx| + |dy|) at 1.5 m/s; can reach outdoor and indoor locations, not roofs. Equipment: cargo carrier (max 10 kg), robotic arm, camera. Endurance: 3600 s, including the return to its start.
- M2 (mobile_manipulator): starts at base. Drives on the road grid (travel distance = |dx| + |dy|) at 1.5 m/s; can reach outdoor and indoor locations, not roofs. Equipment: cargo carrier (max 7 kg), robotic arm, camera. Endurance: 2580 s, including the return to its start.
- D2 (quadcopter): starts at base. Flies in straight lines at 9 m/s; can reach outdoor and roof locations, not indoor ones. Equipment: camera, cargo carrier (max 2 kg). Endurance: 1200 s, including the return to its start.
- G1 (rover): starts at base. Drives on the road grid (travel distance = |dx| + |dy|) at 2 m/s; can reach outdoor and indoor locations, not roofs. Equipment: cargo carrier (max 22 kg), camera, thermal camera. Endurance: 5400 s, including the return to its start.

Tasks:
- T1: Deliver the toolkit (4 kg) to control room. Location: control room. Duration: 30 s. Needs: cargo carrier (payload 4 kg).
- T2: Tighten the valve at parking lot. Location: parking lot. Duration: 240 s. Needs: robotic arm. Can start only after T7 is finished.
- T3: Photograph parking lot for the condition report. Location: parking lot. Duration: 90 s. Needs: camera. Deadline: finished by t = 180 s.
- T4: Replace the filter cartridge at workshop. Location: workshop. Duration: 180 s. Needs: robotic arm.
- T5: Deliver the pressure gauge (14 kg) to gate 2. Location: gate 2. Duration: 60 s. Needs: cargo carrier (payload 14 kg).
- T6: Deliver the pressure gauge (2 kg) to gate 2. Location: gate 2. Duration: 60 s. Needs: cargo carrier (payload 2 kg).
- T7: Deliver the battery pack (5 kg) to parking lot. Location: parking lot. Duration: 30 s. Needs: cargo carrier (payload 5 kg).
- T8: Tighten the valve at water tank. Location: water tank. Duration: 120 s. Needs: robotic arm.
- T9: Replace the filter cartridge at control room. Location: control room. Duration: 180 s. Needs: robotic arm. Can start only after T1 is finished.
- T10: Deliver the replacement filter (11 kg) to workshop. Location: workshop. Duration: 30 s. Needs: cargo carrier (payload 11 kg).

Rules:
1. Every task is done by exactly one robot. A robot does its tasks one at a time, in the order you list them, travelling between task locations.
2. A robot can only do a task if it has the needed equipment, enough payload capacity, and can reach the task location.
3. A task that must start after another task waits until that task is finished, even if a different robot does it.
4. Each robot must be back at its start location before its endurance runs out.
5. Every task must be finished by t = 1200 s.

Objective: minimise the finish time of the last task (the makespan).
briefs.informal:
Morning! Plan for today's site work:

Positions are in metres from the base at (0, 0). Drones fly straight and can't go indoors; ground robots follow the road grid (so they travel |dx| + |dy|) and can't get onto roofs. Everyone leaves their start spot at time zero.

Places: warehouse roof (-8, 99, a rooftop); office roof (65, 143, a rooftop); control room (-59, -3, indoors); workshop (-129, -147, indoors); gate 2 (85, 42, outside); water tank (-41, -33, outside); parking lot (138, 139, outside).

The fleet: D1 is a quadcopter at base with a camera and a thermal camera; it flies at 8.5 m/s, can lift 2 kg, and its battery lasts 15 minutes including the flight home. M1 is our mobile manipulator at base: gripper arm, camera, room for 10 kg, moves at 1.5 m/s and lasts 60 minutes including getting back. M2 is our mobile manipulator at base: gripper arm, camera, room for 7 kg, moves at 1.5 m/s and lasts 43 minutes including getting back. D2, a quadcopter waiting at base, carries a camera, cruises at 9 m/s, lifts up to 2 kg and has 20 minutes of flight time, return trip included. G1 is a rover parked at base that hauls up to 22 kg at 2 m/s and runs for 90 minutes including the drive back. It has a camera and a thermal camera.

Jobs:
(T1) Control room needs the toolkit, which weighs 4 kg - that takes 0.5 minutes on site.
(T2) The valve at parking lot needs tightening - that takes 4 minutes on site but only once the battery pack (T7) has arrived.
(T3) Grab photos of parking lot for the condition report - that takes 1.5 minutes on site and it has to be finished within the first 3 minutes.
(T4) Change the filter at workshop - that takes 3 minutes on site.
(T5) Gate 2 needs the pressure gauge, which weighs 14 kg - that takes 1 minute on site.
(T6) Drop the pressure gauge off at gate 2; it weighs 2 kg - that takes 1 minute on site.
(T7) Parking lot needs the battery pack, which weighs 5 kg - that takes 0.5 minutes on site.
(T8) The valve at water tank needs tightening - that takes 2 minutes on site.
(T9) Swap the filter cartridge at control room - that takes 3 minutes on site but only once the toolkit (T1) has arrived.
(T10) Workshop needs the replacement filter, which weighs 11 kg - that takes 0.5 minutes on site.

Everything has to be wrapped up within 20 minutes of the start, and the sooner the last job finishes, the better. Every robot has to make it back to where it started before its battery runs out.
